title: Accounts and ownership ledger
description: Per-account session pointers plus a ledger of every provisioned resource. This ledger is what turns 'changed an ID, got a 200' into a provable access-control finding — without a recorded expected-access set, a 200 proves nothing.

target_version.description: Exact product version the rig runs. Findings must reproduce on a currently maintained release — Elastic maintains the two newest minors — so a run provisioned on a stale rig is unpayable and nothing downstream would otherwise notice.

mode.description: api = self-hosted target provisioned through its own admin API. saas = live third-party signup, which the agent cannot perform and must hand to the user.

role.description: The privilege tier this account is meant to represent. Must be a role a real low-privilege user could hold — an attacker account quietly given extra privilege invalidates every finding built on it.

identity.description: Username / email / user id as the target knows it. Never a password.

ref.description: Pointer to where the material lives (env var name, browser profile id, gitignored file path). Never the secret itself — this file is committed.

provisioned_by.description: agent = created through the target's admin API. user = the user completed signup, because account creation and password entry are not actions the agent performs.

resources.description: At least one resource per resource type per account. Cross-account access attempts are scored against expected_access. An empty ledger cannot prove anything, so at least one entry is required.

expected_access.description: Per-operation, not per-account. Access control is not flat: an attacker sharing a space may legitimately READ a victim's monitor and must not DELETE it. A flat account list forces a choice between manufacturing a false positive on the legitimate read and silently absolving the unauthorized delete — the second discards exactly the finding shape that scored 8.1 here. Any account/operation pair not listed is expected to be denied.

operations.description: What this account is legitimately allowed to do. Anything outside this list succeeding is the finding.

basis.description: Where the assertion came from — doc URL or privileges-reference section. Derived from the product's documented model, never from observed behaviour: if observed access already exceeds documented access, that is the finding, not a reason to widen the ledger.

scope.description: Space / tenant / org the resource lives in, where the target has such a concept.
